name: Congenital sideroblastic anemia-B-cell immunodeficiency-periodic fever-developmental delay syndrome
aliases: Congenital sideroblastic anemia with immunodeficiency and neurodevelopmental delay

criteria.description: Presence of congenital sideroblastic anemia confirmed by bone marrow ring sideroblasts
Documented B-cell immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinemia and recurrent infections
Recurrent episodes of unexplained periodic fever without infectious cause
Global developmental delay affecting motor and cognitive milestones
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with sideroblastic anemia and immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital sideroblastic anemia, B-cell immunodeficiency, periodic fever episodes, and developmental delay
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by laboratory and genetic findings; exclusion of other causes is essential

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic finding on bone marrow biopsy
searchTerms: ring sideroblasts in bone marrow cells
bone marrow cells with iron rings

pathognomonic.notes: Fever episodes typically last several days and recur periodically
searchTerms: repeated fever attacks of unknown origin

pathognomonic.notes: Marked reduction in immunoglobulin levels and circulating B cells
searchTerms: low antibody levels with few B cells

common.notes: Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
searchTerms: global delay in growth and skills

common.notes: Anemia with small, pale red blood cells
searchTerms: anemia with small, light-colored red cells

common.notes: Poor growth and weight gain in infancy and early childhood
Mild to moderate enlargement of the spleen

occasional.notes: Mild liver enlargement noted in some patients
Enlarged lymph nodes during fever episodes
Reduced muscle tone observed in some affected children
Fungal infections of skin and mucous membranes
Iron deposition in the liver detected by biopsy or imaging

rare.notes: Peripheral nerve involvement reported in isolated cases

laboratory: Bone marrow biopsy showing ring sideroblasts
Microcytic hypochromic anemia with elevated serum iron and ferritin
Elevated inflammatory markers during fever episodes
imaging: Liver ultrasound may show hepatomegaly or iron overload
Echocardiogram to evaluate for cardiomyopathy if clinically indicated
other: Clinical observation of recurrent periodic fever without infectious etiology

redFlags: Severe recurrent infections refractory to standard treatment
references: Orphanet: Congenital sideroblastic anemia-B-cell immunodeficiency-periodic fever-developmental delay syndrome, ORPHA:369861
Recent reviews on congenital sideroblastic anemias and combined immunodeficiencies
Case reports describing clinical and genetic features of the syndrome
